candidates.why: The three static globals are freed at 12851-12853 on the normal path, but the same globals are freed again at 12864-12866 on the `error:` path. If control ever reaches `error:` after the normal-path frees (e.g. via a later `goto error`), free_array_hdls dereferences already-freed pointers (hdls->nitems at 740) and frees the same buffers twice. The globals are never set to NULL after free (only initialized at 69-71), so nothing prevents the double free.

free_array_hdls frees the struct at 745 but the caller (12851-12853, 12864-12866) leaves the static globals pointing at the freed memory. Any subsequent use of these globals — e.g. resolve_postponed_header_refs at 12756/12847 reading header_hdls->nitems (12399-12400), resolve_postponed_eed_refs at 12757 reading eed_hdls->nitems (12598), or resolve_postponed_object_refs at 12848 reading obj_hdls->nitems (12450) — would be a use-after-free if reached after a free. The dangling globals are never cleared.

array_push reallocs at 710-711 and on failure returns NULL (715) without freeing the old buffer; the caller assigns the NULL back into the global (e.g. 1200, 1754, 9147, 11055). The original allocation is then leaked and the global becomes NULL, so later dereferences such as header_hdls->nitems (12399) / obj_hdls->nitems (12450) / eed_hdls->nitems (12598) would be NULL-deref rather than UAF — but the lost old pointer means the buffer is unreachable while still referenced conceptually. Reported as suspicious pointer-lifetime handling around the realloc.
